history.summary: Patan Devi (Maa Patneshwari) is the oldest and one of the most sacred temples of Patna, regarded as one of the 51 Siddha Shakti Peethas: Puranic legend says the right thigh of Devi Sati fell here when Vishnu dismembered her corpse with the Sudarshan Chakra. There are two shrines in old Patna city — Badi Patan Devi (Maharajganj area) and Chhoti Patan Devi (Chowk area), the latter considered older; pilgrims commonly visit both. The main black-stone idols represent Mahakali, Mahalakshmi and Mahasaraswati, said to have protected Putraka, founder of Pataliputra. The name of the city Patna is widely believed to derive from Patan Devi, though some derive it from 'patan' (town). The site is also a major centre of Tantrik and Shakti worship.

name: Patan Devi Temple
town_description: Patna is the capital of Bihar, one of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world — ancient Pataliputra, seat of the Mauryan and Gupta empires. It stands on the southern bank of the Ganga and blends ancient heritage (Kumhrar, Agam Kuan) with modern institutions. The city is a major pilgrimage hub with Patna Sahib (Sikh), Patan Devi and Mahavir Mandir drawing devotees year-round.
